ORIGINAL USMLE-STYLE PRACTICE

Suppurative tissue destruction

A febrile patient has a tender fluctuant skin lesion. Drainage yields pus, and microscopy shows abundant neutrophils with loss of the normal tissue architecture. Which mechanism most directly produces this pattern of local destruction?

  1. Enzymatic digestion by inflammatory cells and microbes
  2. Preservation of proteins by widespread denaturation alone
  3. Calcium binding to released adipose fatty acids
  4. Deposition of immune complexes exclusively in vessel walls
  5. Orderly fragmentation of individual cells without leakage
Answer and explanation

Enzymatic digestion by inflammatory cells and microbes

Hydrolytic enzymes liquefy tissue within a bacterial abscess.

Option explanations

Enzymatic digestion by inflammatory cells and microbes: Hydrolytic enzymes liquefy tissue within a bacterial abscess.

Preservation of proteins by widespread denaturation alone: Preservation is characteristic of coagulative rather than suppurative liquefactive necrosis.

Calcium binding to released adipose fatty acids: This describes fat saponification.

Deposition of immune complexes exclusively in vessel walls: This points toward fibrinoid vascular injury.

Orderly fragmentation of individual cells without leakage: That describes apoptosis rather than pus-producing necrosis.
